title: Noetherian analytic local rings and the canonical algebraic completion comparison
statement:
Let $X$ be a separated smooth scheme of finite type over $\mathbf C$, and let $\pi:(M,\mathcal O_M)\to(X,\mathcal O_X)$ be the analytification morphism of ringed spaces of [lem-sfb-smooth-analytification-cotangent]. For $a\in M$ put $x=\pi(a)$, $A=\mathcal O_{X,x}$ and $B=\mathcal O_{M,a}$, and let $\phi:A\to B$ be the map sending a germ of a regular function to its holomorphic germ. Then $A$ and $B$ are Noetherian local rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], with maximal ideals $\mathfrak m$ and $\mathfrak n$, and $\phi$ is local, meaning $\phi^{-1}(\mathfrak n)=\mathfrak m$. The induced map on maximal-ideal-adic completions [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]
$$\widehat\phi:\widehat A=\varprojlim_{r\geq1}A/\mathfrak m^r\longrightarrow\widehat B=\varprojlim_{r\geq1}B/\mathfrak n^r$$
is an isomorphism of rings. It is the map induced by $\phi$ on the quotient systems, so its composite with $A\to\widehat A$ is $A\xrightarrow{\phi}B\to\widehat B$.

source.place: WANTED: Serre, Géométrie algébrique et géométrie analytique, local-ring and completion comparison used in §9 Proposition 10 (the exactness input cited by the parent); the document is absent locally. Analytic Noetherianity is the Weierstrass local-ring theorem.

proof.text: First prove the algebraic Noetherian assertion. Apply [lem-trf-affine-chart-stalk-differentials] to the smooth structure morphism $X\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf C$, which is locally of finite presentation. It supplies an affine neighbourhood $W=\operatorname{Spec}R_0$ of $x$ with $R_0$ finitely presented over $\mathbf C$ and $A\cong(R_0)_{\mathfrak p}$. The field $\mathbf C$ is Noetherian, since its only ideals are zero and the whole field. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] makes $R_0$ Noetherian, and [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian] makes $A$ Noetherian. The localization is local by [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. The complex point $a$ evaluates $R_0$ in $\mathbf C$ with kernel $\mathfrak p$; constants make this evaluation surjective. It extends to $A$ with kernel its maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ and residue field $\mathbf C$.

source.place: Tags 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence), 00FM (section-Noetherian); affine stalk localization as in the cited chart lemma

proof.text: Since $X$ is smooth over $\mathbf C$, [sbc-thm-etale-local-normal-form] gives an affine neighbourhood $U_1$ of $x$ and a morphism $t=(t_1,\ldots,t_d):U_1\to\mathbf A^d_{\mathbf C}$ that is etale in the sense of [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]: smooth, with fibre of dimension $0$ at every point, in particular at $x$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-near-point-smooth-zero-fibre-dimension] there is an open $U'\subseteq U_1$ containing $x$ on which $t$ is etale in the sense of [def-weil-etale-morphism] (locally of finite presentation, flat and unramified). Choose a principal affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq U'$ of the affine scheme $U_1$ containing $x$; these three properties restrict along the open immersion $U\subseteq U'$, so $t|_U$ is etale in that sense, and this $U$ and $t$ are used below and in step 7. Put $c_i=t_i(a)$ and $s_i=t_i-c_i$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-map-iff-etale-affine], $\mathbf C[T_1,\ldots,T_d]\to R$ has zero relative differential module and zero first cotangent homology. Apply [lem-trf-formally-etale-differentials-base-change] to this map over $\mathbf C$, and [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-kahler-basis] to the polynomial algebra. They give the basis $dt_1,\ldots,dt_d$ of $\Omega_{R/\mathbf C}$. The affine description in [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf] makes this a frame of $\Omega^1_{X/\mathbf C}|_U$.

The cotangent comparison in [lem-sfb-smooth-analytification-cotangent] sends that frame to $d_{\mathrm{hol}}t_i^{\mathrm{an}}$. Consequently the holomorphic map $q=(s_i^{\mathrm{an}})_i$ has invertible derivative at $a$: in any manifold chart its component differentials are a basis of the cotangent space. Its components and tuple are analytic by the analytification statement and [lem-sfb-complex-analytic-function-operations]. Apply [lem-sfb-complex-analytic-inverse-toolkit] in the chosen chart, shrinking the inverse neighbourhood using its clause (4), to obtain mutually inverse holomorphic maps between a neighbourhood of $a$ and a neighbourhood of $0\in\mathbf C^d$. Composition with $q$ and its inverse identifies $B$ with $G_d$, the ring of holomorphic germs at $0$ defined in [lem-sfb-holomorphic-germ-taylor-jets]. Under this identification $\phi(s_i)$ is exactly the coordinate germ $z_i$.

source.place: Serre GAGA no.6 Proposition 3, printed pp.9-10, smooth-coordinate expansion; read online; document absent locally

proof.text: Prove $G_e$ Noetherian for all $e\geq0$ by induction, hence for $e=d$. The base $G_0=\mathbf C$ is a field. Suppose $G_{e-1}$ is Noetherian and $I\subseteq G_e$ is an ideal. For $I=0$ use the empty generating set. Otherwise choose nonzero $f\in I$ and use [lem-sfb-holomorphic-weierstrass-division] to change linear coordinates so that $h=f\circ L$ is regular in the last variable, of order $k$. Composition with $L$ and $L^{-1}$ gives inverse ring maps on germs by [lem-sfb-complex-analytic-function-operations], so finite generation of the changed ideal $I\circ L$ suffices. Rename it $I$, so $h\in I$. Let $N\subseteq G_{e-1}^k$ consist of the coefficient tuples of polynomials $r(z,w)$ of degree less than $k$ in $w$ that belong to $I$. This is a submodule: addition and multiplication by germs independent of $w$ preserve $I$. The inductive hypothesis and [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite] give finitely many generators of $N$, represented by $r_1,\ldots,r_m\in I$. For any $g\in I$, analytic division gives $g=qh+r$; since $r=g-qh\in I$, its tuple belongs to $N$, so $r=\sum b_j(z)r_j$. Thus $I=(h,r_1,\ldots,r_m)$. This also works for $k=0$: the zero module has no remainder generators and division gives $I=(h)$. The induction proves $G_d$, and therefore $B$, Noetherian.

source.place: WANTED locally. F. Bruhat, Cartan seminar 1951-52 exp.11, section 2, Theorem 2, printed pp.2-3; division-and-remainder induction read online https://www.numdam.org/item/SHC_1951-1952__4__A11_0.pdf

proof.text: Evaluation at the origin on $G_d$ is onto $\mathbf C$. A germ with nonzero value has a holomorphic reciprocal by [lem-sfb-complex-analytic-function-operations]; a germ with zero value cannot be a unit, since evaluation preserves products and $1$. Hence its kernel $\mathfrak q$ is the unique maximal ideal. Transport along the chart of step 3 to conclude that $B$ is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak n$ the germs vanishing at $a$. By the evaluation description of $\pi$ in [lem-sfb-smooth-analytification-cotangent], $\phi(f)(a)$ equals the residue of $f\in A$ in $\mathbf C$. Thus $\phi^{-1}(\mathfrak n)=\mathfrak m$. In particular $\phi(\mathfrak m^r)\subseteq\mathfrak n^r$ for each $r\geq1$, so $\phi$ induces the compatible quotient maps defining $\widehat\phi$.

source.place: Serre GAGA no.6 Proposition 3, printed pp.9-10, smooth-coordinate expansion; read online; document absent locally

proof.text: Put $P=\mathbf C[T_1,\ldots,T_d]$ and $J=(T_1,\ldots,T_d)$. By [lem-sfb-holomorphic-germ-taylor-jets] and the chart of step 3, evaluation $T_i\mapsto\phi(s_i)$ gives compatible isomorphisms $P/J^r\cong B/\mathfrak n^r$. Their inverse limit is an isomorphism: apply the inverses componentwise to compatible sequences, and compatibility follows by applying the injective isomorphisms at the smaller index. Identify $\varprojlim_rP/J^r$ with $\mathbf C[[T_1,\ldots,T_d]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series] explicitly: a formal series maps to its polynomial truncations of total degree less than $r$; conversely its coefficient at $T^\alpha$ is the coefficient in any truncation with $r>|\alpha|$. A class modulo $J^r$ has a unique such polynomial representative, since $J^r$ consists of polynomials all of whose monomials have degree at least $r$. The two constructions are inverse and preserve sums and Cauchy products. We obtain an isomorphism $\theta_B:\mathbf C[[T]]\to\widehat B$ whose $r$th component is $\sum_{|\alpha|<r}a_\alpha\phi(s)^\alpha\bmod\mathfrak n^r$.

source.place: Serre GAGA no.6 Proposition 3, printed pp.9-10, smooth-coordinate expansion; read online; document absent locally

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-etale-chart-rational-point-taylor-iso] to the chart $t:U\to\mathbf A^d_{\mathbf C}$ of step 2, with $k=L=\mathbf C$ and $b=x$. Its residue-field hypothesis holds by step 1. The base change by the identity field extension is canonically $U$. It gives an isomorphism $\theta_A:\mathbf C[[T_1,\ldots,T_d]]\to\widehat A$ whose image modulo $\mathfrak m^r$ of a series $\sum a_\alpha T^\alpha$ is $\sum_{|\alpha|<r}a_\alpha s^\alpha$. This uses the actual coordinate germs $s_i$, not merely an abstract isomorphism with a power-series ring.

source.place: Tag 039M, lemma-characterize-etale-completions and the following residue-degree remark; polynomial completion calculation in the cited Taylor-isomorphism node

proof.text: For any formal series $F=\sum a_\alpha T^\alpha$ and every $r\geq1$, the $r$th component of $\widehat\phi(\theta_A(F))$ is $\sum_{|\alpha|<r}a_\alpha\phi(s)^\alpha\bmod\mathfrak n^r$, because the quotient map is induced by $\phi$. Step 6 identifies this with the $r$th component of $\theta_B(F)$. Equality of compatible sequences proves $\widehat\phi\circ\theta_A=\theta_B$, hence $\widehat\phi=\theta_B\circ\theta_A^{-1}$ is an isomorphism. For $f\in A$ the $r$th component of both $\widehat\phi(f\bmod\mathfrak m^r)_r$ and the image of $\phi(f)$ in $\widehat B$ is $\phi(f)\bmod\mathfrak n^r$. This proves the required canonical square. When $d=0$ the same argument has no variables and all truncations are $\mathbf C$; the empty scheme has no $a$ to check.
